C_recheck_fix_round.not_fixed_in_script: paper_arm.sh is left as round 8 ran it (commit 9c58d9f), so its weak checks and the broken self-telemetry query remain in the committed script. The recheck script is the verdict-bearing checker for rounds 6 and 8.

comparison_reading: On the same Dagu workload (round 4; round 2 agrees) both contested sets' components worked in their roles: c14 collector ingested Dagu's native spans and step logs; c5 Prometheus and c6 Loki (Claude set) stored and served them, kept pre-kill data across kill -9 and served it again from a restic-restored copy; c8 restic (Codex set) produced a clean hot snapshot of the Dagu run history and both stores with a byte-identical Dagu history restore; c3 sandbox-runtime (Codex set) denied a Dagu step's egress by default. The two sets cover different scope terms (telemetry storage/query vs backup and worker confinement) rather than competing for one role; this receipt records the executed results and does not re-judge the ledger row. Paper-runtime arm (round 8, synthetic broker port): the same five components carried the adaptive-paper runtime's own native path (NautilusTrader node, 16 native fills, flat, SQLite WAL journal) as a sandboxed Dagu step. Loki (Claude set) stored all 300 runtime lines exactly across kill -9 and restic restore once filelog offsets were persisted (file_storage). Without that, rounds 4 and 6 re-ingested every line after a collector restart. LogQL count_over_time matched the step log at every stage. Prometheus (Claude set) retained and served Dagu span metrics and the log-derived counters across kill and restore, but the count-connector counter undercounted by 2 of 300 in round 8, and in round 6 it undercounted intents (16 of 20) after passing through delta_to_cumulative; round 7's alternative exporter path was worse. restic (Codex set) took a hot snapshot of the live WAL journal mid-run (integrity ok) and a cold backup whose restore was byte-identical, with journal table counts equal to the runtime's own counts. srt (Codex set) ran the runtime with egress, out-of-scope writes and a decoy read all denied, while the unsandboxed controls succeeded. The two sets still cover different scope terms. The one role-level weakness found is on the metrics side of the Claude set: log-derived counters through the collector. It does not affect span metrics or Loki queries.
remaining: Real paper-account telemetry and backup of a broker-session order journal. Not run here or in #87. The real runner (runner.py main, scheduled_trial.sh) loads Alpaca paper credentials and calls the broker, and both are prohibited for this unit. The executed substitute is the same runtime's native path against the repository's synthetic SimulatedPort (rounds 5-8). Owner: peer session sota-workflow-resolution.
Ledger re-judgement: catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json row observability-hosting is still pending_lanes on origin/main. Applying #87 and this receipt is a ledger change reserved to the coordinator.

Count-connector counter accuracy: log-derived Prometheus counters undercounted (round 8: 298 of 300; round 6: 16 of 20 intents), and collector self-telemetry recorded no drop. The root cause is not isolated. A fix candidate is a Prometheus self-scrape plus a longer flush window, or deriving the counters in Loki (the LogQL count_over_time was exact).

Scale and durability depth: one run per round (30 s, 6 symbols, at most 20 fills), one kill -9 with nothing in flight, local restic repositories only, srt default-style settings on one runtime step, and no trace backend (traces only as span metrics).
evidence_class_note: Dagu arm: native upstream binaries executed on this host with every run listener on 127.0.0.1 in rounds 3-4 (Loki listened on all interfaces in rounds 1-2, disclosed); a trading-shaped but synthetic DAG; no broker or paper account. Part A is source review of #87's native_proven receipt. Part C (paper arm, rounds 5-8) is local_integration: native upstream binaries and the project's own runtime path, but a synthetic broker port, so it is not paper-account evidence.
limits: The DAG's steps echo trading-shaped marker lines; it is not the project's real Dagu research/paper DAG, so volume and cardinality are toy-sized.

Paper arm: the broker side is repository fixture simulation.SimulatedPort. By its own docstring it models no queue priority, impact, fees or disconnect fills. Telemetry volume is about 300 lines per run.

Paper arm telemetry is the runtime's event sink (controller.events) streamed to stdout as JSON lines by the driver paper_sim_workload.py. The runtime has no OTLP exporter, and Nautilus stdout logging is ERROR-only in build_node.
Paper arm used the existing pinned env adaptive-paper-20260921 read-only instead of a fresh venv under the gap-wave2 cache. Its versions are printed in each round's steps.txt.
Network: each of rounds 6-8 made one unsandboxed HTTPS GET to example.com as the egress control (status 200). No other network calls; no downloads.

Rounds 5-8 scratch data remains under $HOME/.cache/gap-wave2-20260923/observability-hosting/paper-arm-{5,6,7,8} (recovery path). Post-hoc Prometheus instances on 127.0.0.1:39092 were started on copies and stopped (0 listeners afterwards).

Rounds 6-8's in-script PASS lines are the detection method: sandbox probes print exit codes, and unsandboxed controls must succeed. Round 6's retention check could not detect duplicates; round 8's exact-count checks could.

paper_arm.sh's in-script checker has the weaknesses listed in results.C_recheck_fix_round (substring exit matches, name-only span checks, timestamp-only Loki checks, no hot-overlap test, broken self-telemetry query). The verdict for rounds 6 and 8 rests on recheck_paper_arm.py over the committed raw files.

Telemetry-store restore is checked by query parity (span values, Loki bodies and pairs, count maxima) only. It is not a sample-by-sample comparison of the full TSDB or Loki chunk history. The byte-identical diff covers the work dir and DAGU_HOME only.
